name: United Arab Emirates

nso.name: Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Centre (FCSC); emirate-level: Statistics Centre - Abu Dhabi (SCAD), Dubai Statistics Center (DSC)

latest_census.notes: The 2005 census is the last full enumeration; it recorded nationality (country of citizenship) and religion, and religion was released nationally only (roughly three-quarters Muslim). The 2010 round was register/estimate-based with no questionnaire, and there has been no census since; population figures are register-based estimates from the FCSC and the emirate statistics centres (SCAD, DSC, Sharjah). 'Ethnicity' here means nationality, and the only subnational split published is citizen / non-citizen.

subnational_sources.title: Population estimates by emirate, nationality (citizens / non-citizens) and sex (FCSC statistical yearbook / SCAD Statistical Yearbook of Abu Dhabi / DSC Population Bulletin)
subnational_sources.evidence: Every UAE statistical yearbook carries population by emirate split into citizens and non-citizens, and the emirate centres publish the same as XLS. It gives an Emirati share per emirate (the packet's 'Emirati 11.6%') but no breakdown of the non-national majority by country or region, so it is a two-category count, not the national record's composition. The 7 emirates equal both the admin1 and admin2 counts.

subnational_sources.title: 2005 census: population by religion (national total only)
subnational_sources.publisher: Ministry of Economy / National Bureau of Statistics (predecessor of FCSC)
subnational_sources.evidence: Religion was tabulated nationally in 2005 and never by emirate; listed to record that a religion-by-emirate table is not known to exist.

tier_reason: The only subnational identity count is citizen versus non-citizen by emirate (7 = admin1 = admin2), in yearbook XLS; religion has only ever been released nationally and language is not collected.
recommended_action: Take the citizen / non-citizen population by emirate from the FCSC or the emirate statistics centres and record it as a nationality register with two categories, if the owner accepts a partial ethnicity composition; otherwise leave ethnicity not_available with a note. Record religion as not_available below national level (asked in 2005, released nationally only) rather than not_collected, and language as not_collected (no census or register item).
summary: The UAE's last full census was 2005; since then population statistics are register estimates from the FCSC and the emirate centres. The only subnational identity split published is citizens versus non-citizens by emirate, available as yearbook XLS and matching the 7 admin1/admin2 shapes, which yields an Emirati share but not the rest of the national ethnicity list. Religion was tabulated nationally in 2005 and never by emirate; language is not collected. Tier B for a partial two-category count.
